After an aggressive expansion that swept through the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again expanding its footprint in San Jose. Here are the details.

Apple continues to expand its real estate portfolio

According to the Mercury News (via AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease an office building of 125,800 square feet at 580 North Mary Avenue in San Jose.

This deal is Apple's first major real estate transaction in the area in 2026. Earlier in 2025, the company had spent more than US$1 billion expanding its footprint in the South Bay.

That expansion included the purchase of the Cupertino Gateway complex, consisting of three buildings, for US$166.9 million; the acquisition of the Mathilda Commons campus in San Jose, consisting of two buildings, for US$350 million; and the purchase of the adjacent Mathilda campus, consisting of four buildings, for US$365 million.

Apple subsequently spent another US$216 million to purchase two buildings on Stevens Creek Boulevard in Cupertino, bringing the company's total Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Returning to this new lease, the Mercury News noted that the deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay begins to pick up, with vacancy rates improving compared with the previous quarter and the same period last year:

According to a Colliers report, the South Bay office vacancy rate was 14.1% in the second quarter of 2026. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

Apart from Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in San Jose.
